transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-04-27 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Stonegate), Tomás Rivera (Stonegate), Lena Brooks (Stonegate)

Summary: Quick hosted API walkthrough showing embeddings endpoint and reranker. Focused on search relevance use case and how Redwood handles scale, caching, and fallbacks.

00:00 Jenna Park: all right hello everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jennapark from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with me is marcus liu who is our se and he'll run through the api and demos
00:22 Priya Nair: hi thanks, i'm priya, lead for search at stonegate, wanted to cover current issues with discovery and how we might improve ranking quality without blowing up costs
00:47 Marcus Liu: cool, yea i'll start with the high level flow - we typically show embeddings -> vector DB retrieval -> rerank, but with Redwood's hosted approach you can call embeddings then our rerank endpoint directly to do cross-encoder scoring, so less glue code
01:15 Tomás Rivera: quick Q, we currently use pinecone + an internal re-ranker, what's the main difference if we move rerank to redwood's hosted endpoint?
01:42 Marcus Liu: great question — two parts: latency & control. Hosted rerank centralizes scoring close to embeddings if you use our managed storage, and we offer batching and KV cache to keep p99 latency low. Also you get fewer moving pieces vs pinecone+external model calls
02:10 Priya Nair: when you say KV cache, do you mean the key-value that's used for lm kv cache or some prefix caching for embeddings? i've seen both terms used
02:34 Marcus Liu: sorry bit of transcription there — we mean prefix/K-V cache at the request layer, so repeated queries or similar prefixes hit the cache and avoid full compute; it's not the transformer kv cache per se, it's a request-level cache
03:01 Lena Brooks: ok can you show the actual api calls? we want to understand the client dev story and how it maps to our current flow
03:25 Marcus Liu: sure, i'll share my screen, first the embeddings endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings with doc text, you get back vectors. then for simple rerank there's POST /v1/rerank with a candidate list and a question/prompt, we return scores + normalized rank. i'll paste examples into the chat
04:12 Marcus Liu: (typing) sample payload: {query: "best hiking boots under 100", candidates: ["doc1","doc2"...]} — implementer note, if you already have candidate ids from your vector DB we can accept ids and fetch vectors server-side
05:01 Tomás Rivera: how do you handle vector dimensionality differences? our current embeddings are 1024-d, some open models are 768-d, will that break the rerank?
05:25 Marcus Liu: short answer: rerank is model-agnostic at the scoring layer — if you pass embeddings we accept vectors, if you pass raw text we compute embeddings with the hosted model. mixing dims isn't ideal if you're doing pure vector similarity in your DB; for rerank we re-embed or we accept your vectors if dims match. we can also recommend a migration quant profile
06:10 Priya Nair: latency numbers? we need p50 ~40-60ms and p95 under 200 for interactive UI, at least for top-5 reranks
06:36 Marcus Liu: on our hosted tier, typical p50 for a 5-candidate rerank is ~30-70ms depending on model size; p95 can be 150-300ms if you hit cold starts, but with caching and warm pools we often keep p95 under 180ms. i'll note those are for our optimized compiled kernels and smaller 7b-ish reranker models
07:12 Jenna Park: to add, we offer dedicated pools if you want stricter SLOs; that's a reserved capacity product but you get consistent p95s and isolation
07:40 Tomás Rivera: cost question — do we pay per token for rerank? we want to avoid token-based explosion given our traffic
08:02 Marcus Liu: good point — rerank pricing usually has two components: compute per call (model size + seq len) and embedding storage/ingest. for typical rerank flows customers see unit costs lower than running an equivalent LLM in a separate endpoint because of batching and optimized kernels. we'll send a pricing example later
08:38 Priya Nair: security — we need SOC 2, SSO (SAML), and customer-managed keys (KMS). also data residency for EU requests
09:05 Jenna Park: we are SOC 2 and can enable SSO. for KMS we integrate with major cloud KMS/HSM and for private deployments we have VPC/on-prem options. i'll attach the SOC2 report and DPA after the call
09:31 Lena Brooks: any gotchas for PII? we have resume text and support tickets with sensitive info
09:45 Marcus Liu: default is transient tokens, you can opt for no-logs mode and redwood private options if you need full control. we'll document retention settings; the DPA covers touchpoints
10:12 Tomás Rivera: demo time?
10:20 Marcus Liu: yep — demo: i'm going to run a live rerank with 8 candidates. note that live runs occasionally have audio lag — bear with me
10:39 Marcus Liu: (screen) curling embeddings... curl POST /v1/embeddings -> returned 8x768 vectors in ~210ms for this sample set
11:05 Marcus Liu: then rerank call... POST /v1/rerank with those vectors and the query. result: we returned scores and a mapped confidence field in 165ms
11:33 Priya Nair: hmm interesting, those docs moved in rank relative to our current heuristic — this looks promising
12:00 Tomás Rivera: do you do any re-ranking feature engineering or is it pure cross-encoder model scoring?
12:20 Marcus Liu: both patterns exist. our rerank supports full cross-encoder scoring, and we also let you surface features (click-rate, recency) to a hybrid ranker. you can combine ML score and business features via a simple weighted function in the request payload
12:55 Jenna Park: also worth pointing out our Optimize tooling — it can suggest batching configs, quantization, and cost/perf tradeoffs based on your workload shape
13:20 Priya Nair: what does Optimize recommend for high-throughput question-answering vs write-heavy indexing?
13:40 Marcus Liu: for QA with many short queries, bigger batches for embeddings and smaller, warm rerank pools are best. for heavy indexing, offline bulk-embed pipelines with dedup caching and quantized embeddings save costs. Optimize will give a report after analyzing a sample workload
14:10 Lena Brooks: can you show what the console looks like for rerank traces? we want to see per-route latency and cost
14:35 Marcus Liu: sure, (screen) console -> routes -> rerank-api -> you can see per-request token counts, latency histogram, tail traces and a replay link. also a comparison between model variants if you run A/B rollouts
15:12 Priya Nair: we'd like a canary rollout to test 10% traffic to rerank before full cutover, any built-in support?
15:30 Marcus Liu: yes, canary and A/B rollouts are in the console. you can define traffic percents and automatic fallback to an older model or a cheaper variant on error rate spikes
16:02 Tomás Rivera: for the pilot, how would capacity look? we expect spikes during marketing drops — can we burst beyond pilot limits?
16:28 Jenna Park: hosted can burst within region limits; if you expect sustained high QPS we'd recommend dedicated pools or a hybrid (hosted baseline + dedicated for spikes)
16:50 Priya Nair: does the rerank accept pre-computed embeddings from us (we might keep embeddings in our existing vector store)?
17:10 Marcus Liu: yes, you can pass vectors or ids. if you pass ids we will fetch from our managed vector store only if you choose to sync. otherwise passing your vectors is supported as long as dims match. slight caveat: scoring behavior can vary if embeddings differ in scale — we typically normalize
17:45 Tomás Rivera: any rate limits? we need to plan client throttling if we use the public endpoint
18:05 Marcus Liu: default rate limits on hosted tier are conservative but adjustable per account. for pilot we'll add a higher rate limit and can throttle at the SDK client or gateway level
18:30 Priya Nair: what about multi-tenant data isolation? we need strict separation for different brands we host
18:52 Jenna Park: hosted provides logical separation; for stricter isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments which provide tenant-level isolation and VPC controls
19:20 Lena Brooks: we've got a long tail of older docs — will rerank degrade if candidate set contains many noisy long sequences?
19:46 Marcus Liu: we do token trimming and sequence bucketing; for long docs we support chunking + rerank subset sampling. also batching helps keep compute efficient
20:10 Priya Nair: i saw mention of quantization profiles — will that affect ranking fidelity?
20:28 Marcus Liu: there's a trade-off; Optimize will recommend which model variants to quantize and to what level. for rerank where relative ordering matters we recommend light quantization and evals on held-out prompts to check regressions
21:05 Tomás Rivera: can we run evaluation harnesses? we have labeled queries and MRR targets
21:30 Marcus Liu: yes we can run your eval set through our test harness, produce MRR/Recall metrics and show delta vs your baseline. Marcus will run an initial pass and include the spreadsheet link
22:02 Jenna Park: i'll add pricing scenarios for hosted vs dedicated and a pilot cost estimate to the doc package
22:30 Priya Nair: what about logging and audit? we need immutable logs for legal review
22:48 Marcus Liu: audit logs are available in the console and exportable; for stricter comp you can enable long-term retention add-on
23:10 Lena Brooks: performance question — do you use custom kernels on GPUs or rely on vendor libs?
23:30 Marcus Liu: we use our compiled runtime with optimized kernels and auto kernel selection across hardware. that is why we can get lower p50s for smaller models and still handle larger ones efficiently
24:05 Priya Nair: any example customers with similar scale?
24:25 Jenna Park: we have a few retail and media customers; i'll share anonymized benchmarks and an example case study in the follow-up
25:00 Tomás Rivera: i noticed in the console you showed a 'fallback policy' — what's the sequence during a fallback?
25:20 Marcus Liu: fallback first tries a cheaper model variant in the same pool, then region fallback, then a cached response. all policies are configurable per-route
26:00 Priya Nair: in terms of SLA, for hosted api what uptime and latency guarantees do you offer?
26:18 Jenna Park: hosted has a standard SLA for availability; for tighter latency SLAs we recommend Dedicated with SLO guarantees in the contract
26:40 Tomás Rivera: does the pilot require any infra changes or just API keys?
26:58 Marcus Liu: pilot can be run with API keys and sample data — no infra changes required. if you want to push private data into our managed store we'd set up a secure transfer mechanism
27:20 Priya Nair: are there any compliance checks for EU data residency?
27:40 Jenna Park: yes we can scope region-specific hosting and include data residency clauses in the DPA. also we can provision EU-only regions for your pilot
28:05 Lena Brooks: let's talk success metrics — what should we define for the 2-week pilot?
28:28 Marcus Liu: recommend: MRR lift on top-10 queries, click-through rate improvement, average query latency, and cost per 1k queries. pick 6-8 representative queries and run A/B for two weeks
29:00 Priya Nair: sounds good — timeline wise we can kick off next week if we get pricing and a pilot agreement
29:18 Jenna Park: great. i'll follow up with the pilot template and pricing. marcus will run the first benchmark with your sample set
29:45 Tomás Rivera: small nit — in the demo i saw a confidence field, how do you compute that?
30:05 Marcus Liu: it's a normalized score from the reranker, optionally calibrated with temperature or post-hoc scaling; we expose it so customers can set thresholds for UI decisions
30:30 Priya Nair: any recommended model families for rerank vs embed? we currently use a c4-like embedder
30:55 Marcus Liu: for embeddings we recommend a dense high-dim model for retrieval and a smaller cross-encoder for rerank; Optimize can recommend exact model families based on evals
31:20 Lena Brooks: integration effort — how long to production for a small pilot?
31:40 Marcus Liu: typical 1-2 weeks to get baseline pilot running: ingest sample docs, hook up vector store or pass vectors, run rerank A/B and evaluate
32:05 Priya Nair: let's talk throttling and backoff — if we see 502s what's best practice?
32:20 Marcus Liu: exponential backoff client-side and use the SDK which handles retries. also set up graceful fallback to a cheap heuristic if rerank fails
32:45 Tomás Rivera: are there SDKs for our stack — node + python?
33:00 Marcus Liu: yes official SDKs for python, node, and go; they include helpers for batching and retry logic
33:25 Priya Nair: any limits on candidate list size? sometimes we have 50 candidates for long-tail ranking
33:45 Marcus Liu: we support larger candidate lists but recommend top-50 only for offline or async rerank; for interactive UI top-10 is ideal to keep latency down
34:10 Jenna Park: quick note — for large candidate sets you can do a two-stage flow: coarse vector filter -> rerank top-k
34:35 Lena Brooks: what's included in the pilot pricing?
34:50 Jenna Park: pilot generally includes X credits for compute, a small dedicated rate bump, and access to the SE for benchmark support. we'll detail this in the follow-up
35:12 Tomás Rivera: curious about model updates — how do rollouts handle model versioning so we don't get sudden regressions?
35:35 Marcus Liu: model versioning is first-class: you pin versions per-route and can do canary rollouts. Optimize can run regression checks on your eval set before traffic shift
36:05 Priya Nair: let's capture the eval metrics we care about: MRR, NDCG@10, latency percentiles, and cost per 1k queries
36:25 Jenna Park: noted — we'll include those in the pilot doc
36:40 Tomás Rivera: small ops question: do you keep request-level logs by default or is it opt-in?
36:55 Marcus Liu: request logs are available but retention is configurable; for PII we can mask or not persist depending on settings
37:20 Lena Brooks: ok last product question: can the reranker use external features from our db at scoring time?
37:38 Marcus Liu: yes, you can pass feature vectors or scalars in the request payload, we combine them server-side in the scoring function
38:05 Priya Nair: i'm concerned about drift — how do we detect rerank model degrading over time?
38:20 Marcus Liu: Optimize monitors quality metrics and can alert on regressions per prompt set; we can set thresholds and auto-create a ticket for rollbacks
38:42 Tomás Rivera: cool. any blockers for pilot sign-up?
38:55 Jenna Park: main ones are DPA/SOC2 review and pilot dataset confirmation — both are manageable.
39:18 Priya Nair: ok we'll pull together the dataset and get back
39:35 Marcus Liu: i'll queue the benchmark and post the spreadsheet link in the follow-up
39:50 Jenna Park: thanks everyone, i'll send the follow-up with docs and pricing. any last Qs?
40:10 Lena Brooks: none from me, thanks for the demo
40:22 Priya Nair: thanks all
40:30 (meeting ends, remaining time used for 1:1 notes)

Notes: Transcription contains minor mis-hears (e.g., 'k v cache' vs KV cache, 'Red wood' vs Redwood). Several references to shared artifacts: benchmark spreadsheet (link posted in chat), SOC2 report, pilot template.
